questions.architecture: Pure core holds: the format change (scoped credits coverage, a files map, lower-cased face key) is pure. All node:fs work stays in packages/cli (pack-import-input/-write/-sessions). The CLI reaches core only via format, sdk and schema. Contracts: the new CLI command and its --json reply are decided in ADR-0206 (accepted) before the code (M18.171) and amended in the same commit (session rotation, read-back loader, upstream credit rule). The reply has a zod schema in output.ts and packages/cli/schemas/pack-import.output.json. The format API growth (ImportedPackOptions.credits, ImportedPack.files) is additive, has an API report and changeset, and is covered by ADR-0206. No file-format version change and no new runtime dependency. Security: no symlink following, no read beyond the listed size, strict ZIP names refused before the witness, decompression bounded by readZip limits, atomic write with a temp sibling, read-back and rename, with a race on -o refused. The folder walk counts files, not directories, toward the 4096 cap, so a tree of many empty directories is walked unbounded in count; local input only, not filed.

findings.evidence: nextRound returns `mine.length - lastPass`, so the round after any pass is r1 again. Delta digest lines: M18.172 has 'r1 pass 1 findings' then 'r1 pass 0 findings' while its body says 'r2 pass'. M18.16 has r1, r2 changes-requested, r3 pass, then 'r1 pass 0 findings' while its body says 'r4 pass'. cp22 F2's argue line said 'reopen if cp23 shows the same drift' and attributed restarts only to re-application on a new base, which neither case is.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of the tracked digest (milestone review, check-reviewed) cannot tell how many rounds a commit took. Because the counter resets after a pass, REVIEW_ROUND_CAP can be sidestepped: pass with minors, change the diff, and the next changes-requested is r1 again, so the round cap stop condition never fires for a commit that keeps changing.
findings.recommendation: Number rounds per task from the first verdict since the task's last landed commit (non-rebind lines), so a post-pass fix continues at rN+1. A re-application on a new base keeps its number and adds 'reapply'. Add harness cases for both and for the cap.

findings.evidence: coldSuccess returns green when `ms` is not finite and `cold.log` is a string without the regex match `/::warning title=cold setup over budget::cold setup (\d+) ms/`. ghSource.coldSetup (ci-runs.mjs:130) does not call hydrateColdStepTimes, which view() uses for gh versions that omit step times. GitHub's job-log download renders workflow commands as '##[warning]<message>' rather than the raw '::warning title=…::' text (not verifiable from this sandbox: log blob 403), so the annotation fallback matches only the test's stub. check-budget prints a positive 'budget: cold setup N ms <= LIMIT ms' line on a within-budget run (check-budget.mjs:156) that last-ci does not require. Also: tests/harness/last-ci.test.mjs:42's title still says 'while it is continue-on-error' (M18.164 reviewer minor).
findings.failure_scenario: On a host whose gh omits step times, or when the REST step name changes, a cold-setup that succeeded only under the by-time exemption (e.g. 664 s > 600 s) prints 'cold-setup green'. That is exactly what M18.164 was written to stop, and M18.157's 'three consecutive runs within the limit' would be misread from last-ci.
findings.recommendation: Call it green only when the duration is known to be within the limit, from the step time or the 'budget: cold setup N ms <=' line. Match the over-budget annotation in both raw and '##[warning]' forms. Report anything else as duration UNKNOWN. Hydrate step times in coldSetup as view() does. Rename the M18.161 test title.

findings.evidence: checkPlaywrightReport reports '<spec> [<project>]: no test ran' for every project when the JSON report has no tests, and never reads the report's top-level `errors`. The cp23 packet shows three legs ('3 of 5000 definitions…', 'SVG sanitizer…', 'imported artwork retains exact licensed fonts offline') red with only 'no test ran' on every project. Reproduced here: the run ends 'Error: Process from config.webServer was not able to start' because `pnpm --filter` refuses a symlinked node_modules, and the gate leg would print only 'no test ran'. Separately, m18-feature-legs' 'exit-failure' stub writes a report, so M18.166's 'no report at all' fallback is not exercised (M18.166 reviewer minor).
findings.failure_scenario: A milestone-wide environmental failure (webServer cannot build or bind, browsers missing) and a spec whose tests are all tagged out of a project give the same red. A final-review agent can neither tell a broken environment from missing coverage nor be pointed at the fix. This is the Playwright half of cp22 F3, which recurring makes a gate gap under review.md R12.
findings.recommendation: When no test ran, print the report's first `errors[].message` line (else the runner's output tail) once per leg instead of repeating 'no test ran' per project. Add harness cases for a report with a global error and for a non-zero Vitest exit that writes no report.
